result.rationale: In zoho-bigin CalendarService, the axios call is replaced by refreshOAuthTokens wrapper; the new refreshOAuthTokens returns fetch's Response when sync is enabled (returns `response` from fetch), while the caller reads `tokenInfo.data`, which only exists on an Axios response. When sync is disabled, the wrapper returns the axios response so `.data` works; when enabled, `.data` is undefined, so refreshed credential processing breaks. Same mismatch pattern applies to other axios callers too.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code wraps the axios call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` (from `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a Fetch `Response` object directly from `fetch()`. However, the code at line 91+ still accesses `tokenInfo.data.error` and `tokenInfo.data.access_token`, which are Axios-specific properties. A Fetch Response doesn't have a `.data` property - it requires `.json()` to be called. This means when credential sync is enabled, the refreshed token data won't be properly processed, causing the credential update to fail silently or error out.
